theme: 3 terms for lists in SwiftUI: the scrolling rows, the repeater and the group

terms.definition: A scrolling view that shows rows of data in a column.
terms.example: Show the notes in a List.

terms.definition: A view that creates one view for each item in a collection.
terms.example: Use ForEach to create a row for every note.
terms.code:
let names = ["Mina", "Jake"]
ForEach(names, id: \.self) { name in
    Text(name)
}

terms.definition: A group of rows with an optional header and footer.
terms.example: Put the pinned notes in their own Section.

video.description:
Learn to explain how to show rows of data in SwiftUI: List, ForEach & Section, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
List - A scrolling view that shows rows of data in a column.
ForEach - A view that creates one view for each item in a collection.
Section - A group of rows with an optional header and footer.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain List, ForEach and Section in English?

dialogue.title: Show the team

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I want to show the team members in a scrolling screen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a List. It shows rows in a column and scrolls by itself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I wrote a Text for every name. That is a lot of code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use ForEach. It creates one view for each item in the array.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The code has `id: \.self`. What does that mean?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It tells ForEach how to identify each item. Here the name is the identity.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if two people have the same name?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then you have a problem. The ids must be unique, so use a real id.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: OK. I also want a header above the names.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wrap the ForEach in a Section, like `Team` in the code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does the List need the Section?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No. But a Section makes the List easier to read.
